headline: Launching a Cleaning Company to 38 Google Ads Leads a Month
summary_line: PPC Guru launched Apexshine Cleaning on Google Ads across Local Services and Search, and in just its second full month the account produced 38 genuine phone and form leads at about $50 each — a 27% increase over its first month, with cost per lead down roughly a quarter.
client_context: Apexshine Cleaning Inc. is a cleaning-services company serving commercial and residential clients across the Greater Toronto Area in Ontario, Canada. The business relies on a steady stream of enquiries — phone calls and quote requests from people and offices that need regular or one-off cleaning. Google Ads reaches those buyers at the moment they search, and because cleaning enquiries come heavily by phone, accurate call tracking is central to the account.
background: Apexshine Cleaning partnered with PPC Guru in mid-2026 to build its Google Ads presence from scratch. The plan was a two-front launch: Google Local Services Ads to capture ready-to-book local demand, plus dedicated Search campaigns split by commercial and residential intent — all measured with proper call and form tracking.
analysis: PPC Guru set up call tracking (ad calls and website calls to the Toronto line) and a lead-form conversion, then separated genuine calls and forms from Google Business Profile map actions so reporting would reflect real enquiries. The account was structured into three parts — Local Services, a Commercial Search campaign and a Residential Search campaign — so budget and messaging could match each type of buyer.
analysis_points: Launch Google Local Services Ads to capture ready-to-book local cleaning demand.
Build separate Commercial and Residential Search campaigns to match distinct buyer intent.
Set up call tracking for ad calls and website calls, plus a lead-form conversion.
Exclude Google Business Profile local actions from the lead count so reporting stays honest.

timeline.what: PPC Guru launch — Local Services plus Commercial and Residential Search live; first full month delivered 30 genuine leads at about $66 each.
38 genuine leads at about $50 each — up 27% on the first month, with cost per lead down roughly a quarter.

challenge: As a brand-new account, Apexshine had to build genuine demand across two very different buyer types — commercial and residential — from a standing start, with no history for bidding to learn from. Cleaning enquiries are also phone-heavy, so capturing calls accurately (and keeping map actions out of the lead count) was essential to steer budget toward real work.

changes.why: Captured ready-to-book local demand and pay-per-lead calls at the top of Search.
Targeted office and business cleaning searches with tailored messaging.
Targeted home-cleaning searches separately so budget matched intent.
Measured phone calls and quote requests — the real enquiries — as conversions.
Kept Google Business Profile map actions out of the lead count so reporting reflected true demand.
Pointed bidding at genuine calls and forms as early data built up.

technical.label: Lead signals
technical.value: Ad calls · Website calls · Lead forms

benchmark: Figures cover the account's first two months on Google Ads, so this is an early launch snapshot rather than a long-run trend. Genuine leads count only real phone calls and form submissions — Google Business Profile map actions are excluded.
gradual: The account improved on every front between its first two months: more genuine leads (30 to 38), a lower cost per lead (about $66 to $50) and a higher conversion rate (about 15% to 21%) as bidding learned from early data across the Local Services and Search campaigns. It is an encouraging launch trajectory, best confirmed as more months complete.

spotlight.title: Why a Local Services + Search Combination Works for Cleaning
spotlight.body: Cleaning buyers split into two very different groups — offices booking recurring commercial contracts and homeowners booking one-off or regular cleans. Running Google Local Services Ads alongside dedicated Commercial and Residential Search campaigns lets the account meet both: Local Services captures pay-per-lead calls from ready-to-book customers, while the two Search campaigns tailor messaging and budget to each intent. Tracking real calls and forms across all three — and excluding map actions — is what keeps the lead count honest and points bidding at genuine bookings.

lessons: Track phone calls as conversions — cleaning enquiries come mostly by phone.
Split commercial and residential intent so budget and messaging match the buyer.
Use Local Services Ads to capture ready-to-book, pay-per-lead demand.
Keep Google Business Profile map actions out of the lead count for honest reporting.
Give a new account a few months before drawing firm conclusions.
why_it_worked: Local Services and Search together covered both ready-to-book and higher-intent search demand.
Commercial and residential campaigns matched budget to distinct buyer types.
Call and form tracking measured real enquiries from the first day of spend.
Cost per lead fell and conversion rate rose as bidding learned from early data.
outcome: In its first two months on Google Ads, Apexshine Cleaning has a fast-improving lead engine: 38 genuine phone and form leads in July 2026 at about $50 each, up 27% on its opening month with cost per lead down roughly a quarter. This is an early launch snapshot on a young account, and the momentum across Local Services and Search gives a strong, data-backed basis to keep scaling as more months complete.
cta: PPC Guru helps Canadian cleaning and home-services companies turn search demand into tracked calls and bookings with Local Services and conversion-focused Search.
methodology: All figures are pulled directly from the client's Google Ads account and shown on a monthly basis. 'Genuine leads' are phone calls and lead-form submissions only; Google Business Profile local actions are excluded. The account has only two months of history (Jun–Jul 2026), so this is an early launch snapshot.
lead_quality: The majority of genuine leads are direct phone calls to the company's Toronto line — the highest-intent enquiry type for a cleaning business — alongside a growing share of online form requests.
